ucas.description: A divergent replica remains eligible without repair.
Healthy copies are demoted on false or correlated failure observations.
A master is demoted before a usable successor exists.
A lone unhealthy master loses its assignment without a successor.
A live node remains Down indefinitely.
An empty or stale node is crowned master.
Multiple processes serve as master for a partition.
A masterless partition is never refilled.
A replica is activated or promoted before completing synchronization.
Deletion destroys the last usable copy.
Deletion interrupts reconstruction or repeats on a terminating pod.
Force deletion bypasses evidence and drain conditions.
Topology application is lost or never retried.
Delayed topology arrives after a newer authority or assignment.
A deposed leader still issues topology commands.
Repeated resync failure never removes an unsafe replica from serving.
Endpoint membership advertises an unserving node.

constraint.text: Only the current leader may issue topology changes; recipients must reject obsolete authority.

controls.title: Authorize topology application
scenarios: An old reconcile resumes after lease takeover; a node has not yet heard the new generation.
assumptions: Lease availability and generation identity must be established; a newer generation fences only recipients that have observed it.
residual_risks: A check before sending cannot close the check/send race: the lease can be lost between the read and the first packet, or while the broadcast is in flight.

Recipient-side version fencing only protects a node that has ALREADY observed the newer generation; a node that missed the new leader's broadcast will accept an older leader's map. Per-node applied-generation tracking is SAF-09.
The post-send lease re-read records that the race occurred; it cannot retract what was sent.

Observed while building CHECK-01, not asserted on: after the lease is deleted and the SAME process re-acquires it, the operator was seen broadcasting a LOWER version than nodes already held, which their fencing rejects. The manipulation is cruder than a real takeover; treat as a lead for SAF-09.
The stop position is a test seam. It is inert without the environment variable and bounded at 120s, but it is production code that a misconfiguration could delay one broadcast with.

A suppressed send is retried only by a process that survives the suppression (lease read failure, momentarily foreign holder): the pending flag is in memory, and a confirmed lease loss ends the process, after which the next leader republishes from its own committed state. The retry test proves the flag was set by the withheld pass and consumed by the pass that published (that pass names the suppressed version); it does not prove the flag was NECESSARY for that send, because the committed version usually moves by itself within a pass.

Liveness (/healthz) is process-alive only and readiness treats a non-leader as ready. The operator that logged 'LOST LEASE -- exiting' and then hung — the Lean runtime waits for the never-ending server tasks before reporting the uncaught error — was therefore never restarted; that defect is fixed (IO.Process.exit) and CHECK-01 asserts the restart count moves, but a different stall of the main loop would still pass both probes.
controls.call_path: runReconcileFSMLoop -> commitClusterState -> (post-commit) lease check -> broadcastTopologyToAllPods. The FSM BroadcastTopology effect, which sent the unmerged map without a leadership check, has been removed; the effect constructor no longer exists.

checks.procedure: Drive the production reconcile to a named stop position (committed, version advanced, pre-send lease check not yet made) using the FLARE_TEST_PRESEND_BARRIER seam, and confirm the position was reached by reading the held version the operator writes there. Topology changes are triggered by patching the FlareCluster readBalance spec (non-destructive). Then, for the same held pass: (a) retain the lease and require the release to broadcast that version - the control that proves the pass reaches the send at all; (b) hand the lease to another identity and require a fence log naming that version with no broadcast, then require the container restart count to move (losing the lease is designed to end the process), the restarted process to log lease acquisition, and the topology to be applied - exactly one Active master, every node Active, each flared's own `stats nodes` naming that master; (c) delete the lease and require the read-failure branch with no broadcast, then a later pass of the SAME process that publishes and names the suppressed version, and the applied topology. A receiver whose version does not move is not accepted as evidence on its own: a crash, a timeout or an exit before the branch look the same. Separately, push a mutated map at a stale version from inside the cluster and require flared both to keep its map and to log the rejection. Every test releases the barrier and restores authority before judging.

review.note: SAF-01 finishing. Three things changed. (1) A suppressed send is now retried: the pending flag records the earliest suppressed version and the publishing pass names it; scope stated in code and in the residuals - it covers only a process that survives the suppression. (2) The takeover test exposed that the operator never actually exited on lease loss: `throw` from main is followed by lean_finalize_task_manager(), which waits for the TCP, health and metrics server tasks, none of which return; the pod stayed Running at RESTARTS 0, passing both probes, owning nothing. Replaced with IO.Process.exit; the test now asserts the restart count moves, the restarted process re-acquires, and the topology is applied (one Active master, all Active, each flared naming it) - not merely that the node count matches. (3) Barrier cleanup is deterministic (release-and-wait, then clear); the trigger is a readBalance patch instead of a pod delete, which had left flared crash-looping while the control plane was held. Failed attempt at 53488c4 is recorded: the retry line was logged only when the version had not moved, so the retry was invisible in a live cluster; that is a logging fix, not a behavior change. Implementation stays PARTIAL (check/send race open, recipient fencing limited to nodes that saw the newer generation - SAF-09). Verification stays UNVERIFIED pending the reviewer's assessment.

constraint.text: mergeClusterState commits at most one Master per partition in its node map.

controls.title: Bound committed master assignments
scenarios: FSM and TCP registration update overlapping snapshots.
assumptions: The claim applies to the committed map, not simultaneously serving flared processes or unmerged outgoing effects.
residual_risks: Independent node maps, delivery loss and old leaders are outside this count property.

The property covers the committed map only. Before SAF-01 an outgoing snapshot could bypass it entirely; that path is removed, but any future send that does not read the committed state would be outside the proof again.

checks.procedure: Elaborate the general commit/count proofs and review that production commits still use the proved functions; separately test outgoing snapshots.

review.note: Main.lean changed in two ways that touch SC-02 only indirectly. The lease-loss path now ends the process (IO.Process.exit) where before it hung with the role label already set to standby and no reconcile loop - a process that neither led nor exited. Commit and merge (commitClusterState, demoteDuplicateMasters) are untouched; the single post-commit send path is unchanged except for the retry flag, which publishes the CURRENT committed map, never a stored older one. No new evidence for SC-02 itself.

constraint.text: A replica with missed writes remains repair-pending until reconstruction completes and missing data is recovered.

controls.title: Repair dropped replica writes
scenarios: Drops during normal service, breaker hold, unmatched destinations, operator restart and master counter reset.
assumptions: Drop counters describe a particular source/destination incarnation; reconstruction must actually reach flared.
residual_risks: Proxy demotion is not broadcast before reassignment; counters are consumed even when repair is skipped, and initial nonzero counts are baselined.
controls.call_path: queue_proxy_write records destination drops -> stats -> Main 4d -> stateRef demotion -> next FSM proxy assignment -> node sync -> role shift.

checks.procedure: Drop selected writes; require actual reconstruction and value recovery without new drops after each blocked/restart case. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

review.note: Main.lean changed for SAF-01 finishing (lease-loss exit, retry of a suppressed send, none of it in the drop-repair block) and the K8sReconciler gained nothing this control relies on. Reconstruction observability is unchanged at this revision. Relevant to SC-03 only in that a suppressed node-sync (which carries the role shift that starts a reconstruction) is now re-sent by a later pass instead of being lost until the version moved again. SAF-02/SAF-05 follow on this branch and will rewrite this entry.

constraint.text: Normal promotion and Prepare activation require a completed usable copy associated with the current source.

controls.title: Require valid synchronization evidence
scenarios: Prepare replica has a small nonzero LSN; source changes while stats are being sampled.
assumptions: Active is an operator designation, not independent proof of complete data; LSNs require matching lineage.
residual_risks: Prepare repair accepts a gap below 5000 without lineage/completion evidence; masterless emergency promotion is a separate exception (SC-06).
controls.call_path: Main 4c stats -> NodeState Active -> reconcileStep; drain/failover -> findActiveSuccessor.

checks.procedure: Reject close-but-incomplete LSNs, mismatched lineage and a changed source; accept only a completed current reconstruction. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

review.note: Main.lean changed for SAF-01 finishing: the lease-loss path now ends the process (IO.Process.exit; `throw` left a pod that neither led nor exited), and a topology send suppressed by the lease fence is retried by a later pass that names the suppressed version. Neither touches the mechanism EV-04 relies on (Require valid synchronization evidence); its code path and claim are unchanged at this revision, and no new evidence is recorded for it.

constraint.text: Delete only a revalidated target when independent current evidence supports the surviving copy.

controls.title: Protect copies before deleting Pods
scenarios: Missing or malformed master stats; resync removes the successor in the same tick; Pod replacement or lease loss before deletion.
assumptions: tmpfs data is lost on Pod deletion; Active-master presence alone is not data-integrity evidence.
residual_risks: Missing curr_items defaults to zero; gates and successor probes use snapshots; graceful deletion does not guarantee successful handoff.
controls.call_path: Main 4d/4e -> podDeletionAllowed -> deletePodGraceful -> subsequent terminating detection/drain.

checks.procedure: Malformed/empty/truncated/stale stats must not delete; combine resync and empty-master repair, concurrent re-registration and leader loss. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

review.note: Main.lean changed for SAF-01 finishing: the lease-loss path now ends the process (IO.Process.exit; `throw` left a pod that neither led nor exited), and a topology send suppressed by the lease fence is retried by a later pass that names the suppressed version. Neither touches the mechanism EV-05 relies on (Protect copies before deleting Pods); its code path and claim are unchanged at this revision, and no new evidence is recorded for it.

constraint.text: Refill missing masters under an explicit emergency policy, with partial-copy promotion distinguished from normal successor promotion.

controls.title: Make emergency refill tradeoffs explicit
scenarios: All copies restart; only a Prepare copy remains; probes fail or return empty data.
assumptions: Availability may deliberately be chosen over completeness; data-bearing means nonzero count, not a complete or newest copy.
residual_risks: Active candidates lack a data check; absent data-bearing observations fall back; Prepare partial copies can become authoritative.
controls.call_path: NodeAdd rejoin -> Slave/Prepare; FSM failover/RecoveryRefill -> promoteMasterlessPartitions -> promoteMasterlessPartition.

checks.procedure: Cover total restart, known empty vs unknown, surviving Active and Prepare copies; document expected loss/availability policy. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

review.note: Impact review only; not worked on. promoteMasterlessPartition is unchanged. Relevant only in that a refill result, including a deliberate partial-copy promotion, is now published once from the committed map rather than also from the FSM's unmerged snapshot - so what nodes are told matches what was committed. The emergency tradeoff itself is unchanged and still undocumented in user-facing terms (SAF-07). CHECK-06 remains unrun.

constraint.text: Use Pod existence/readiness streaks with guards, retaining an unhealthy lone master rather than stripping its assignment.

controls.title: Use qualified failure observations
scenarios: Pod disappears, CrashLoopBackOff, process hang with listening socket, correlated worker failure.
assumptions: Kubernetes observations can lag; unknown input must not become an empty Pod list; readiness is partly circular.
residual_risks: Parallel string lists conflate observations; nodeName is unused; Ready does not prove data health.
controls.call_path: ListPods -> executeK8sRequest -> PodListResponse -> detectDeadNodesPure -> unhealthyMastersKept -> failover.

checks.procedure: Exercise missing pods, sustained NotReady, failed API listing, lone unhealthy master and multiple pods on a lost worker. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

Neither touches the mechanism EV-07 relies on (Use qualified failure observations); its code path and claim are unchanged at this revision, and no new evidence is recorded for it.

constraint.text: The pure drain transform retains a master assignment if there is no Active slave successor.

controls.title: Keep drain assignments without a successor
scenarios: Terminating master with only Prepare slaves, or its sole slave drained first.
assumptions: The bound is on the transform, not on data completeness or Pod survival through its termination grace period.
residual_risks: External deletion still finishes; an Active successor may be stale and delivery may fail.
controls.call_path: detectDrainingNodesPure -> handleDrainWithPromotion -> drainBlockedKeys -> Main drainNoSuccessor metric.

checks.procedure: Test no successor, Prepare-only successor and both drain orders; assert the master remains assigned and the blocked signal is raised. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

review.note: Impact review only; not worked on. The drain transform and drainBlockedKeys are unchanged. The retained-master case commits no change, so as with EV-07 it now produces no send at all; the drainNoSuccessor metric, not the wire, remains the signal. CHECK-08 remains unrun.

constraint.text: Circuit-breaker policy pauses mass failover; configured recovery refill is a separate path.

controls.title: Limit mass-failure changes
scenarios: Many Active nodes become dead candidates; hysteresis holds; auto-reset disabled.
assumptions: Breaker thresholds use observed Active/dead population, not actual data health.
residual_risks: Correlated worker faults are not modeled explicitly; autoResetEnabled=false parks refill.
controls.call_path: AfterDetectDead computes breaker state -> EmergencyPaused or RecoveryRefill; trippedRef carries hysteresis.

checks.procedure: Run breaker scenarios including auto-reset disabled and recovery refill; confirm no unintended mass demotion. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

review.note: Impact review only; not worked on. Breaker policy and hysteresis are unchanged. SAF-01 does touch the tripped path indirectly: RecoveryRefill previously also published through the pre-commit effect, and now publishes only via the post-commit send, which is lease-checked. Recovery while tripped is therefore now subject to the same authority check as normal operation - intended, and not separately tested. CHECK-09 remains unrun.

constraint.text: Restart a stuck Proxy/Down only when current safety evidence permits deleting its copy.

controls.title: Recover stuck Down without losing data
scenarios: A live process remains Down; terminating pod remains on an unreachable worker.
assumptions: One-per-tick deletion and mapped Active masters are preliminary gates, not evidence of a usable surviving copy.
residual_risks: Deletion gates share stale-state/data-validity weaknesses with empty-master repair.
controls.call_path: Main 4e counts present non-terminating Down pods -> podDeletionAllowed -> graceful deletion -> NodeAdd rejoin.

checks.procedure: Keep unsafe or terminating copies; restart only eligible stuck Down pods and verify data after rejoin. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

constraint.text: Expose masterless, unhealthy, unreachable, drain-blocked and resync-failure signals; reachability loss alone does not cause failover.

controls.title: Detect failures without inventing recovery
scenarios: Kept unhealthy master; operator-only network partition; repeated flared resync failure.
assumptions: Chart rules must be enabled, scraped and routed in the deployment for an operational alert claim.
residual_risks: No deployment/run evidence is archived here; flared request_down_node cannot self-demote through the absent flarei controller.
controls.call_path: Main observations and flared stats -> metrics -> chart Prometheus rules -> deployment-specific routing; probe failures are alert-only.

checks.procedure: Assert per-partition masterless and retained-master alerts, operator partition behavior and actual routed alert receipt. Treat self-demotion test skips as missing evidence. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

constraint.text: Count comparison detects some replica divergence; content equality requires additional verification.

controls.title: Detect content divergence
scenarios: Missing and extra keys cancel; equal keys have different values; multiple replicas diverge.
assumptions: curr_items is coarse and the current probe selects one Active slave per master.
residual_risks: Equal counts cannot establish key/value equality; content anti-entropy is absent.
controls.call_path: Main 4d stats -> replicaKeyDelta; master mutation paths -> proxy writes to replicas.

checks.procedure: Inject missing/extra keys with equal counts and differing values; measure detection/repair coverage and all-replica coverage. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

Neither touches the mechanism EV-12 relies on (Detect content divergence); its code path and claim are unchanged at this revision, and no new evidence is recorded for it.

constraint.text: A future replication design must specify what acknowledged writes survive and how replicas catch up after interruption.

controls.title: Bound replication durability guarantees
scenarios: Replica unavailable through WAL retention; asynchronous drop after client success; master failover.
assumptions: Current live replication is op-level forwarding; WAL is used for reconstruction/bootstrap only.
residual_risks: No continuous WAL replication; adding master LSNs alone does not establish durable acknowledgement semantics.
controls.call_path: Client write -> proxy queue; recovery -> handler_reconstruction -> op_repl_sync_wal; these are distinct paths.

checks.procedure: Compare candidate designs against acknowledged-write survival, expiry/delete propagation, replica reads and migration compatibility. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

review.note: Initial static audit. Existing code and prospective checks are not archived execution evidence; no safety verification is claimed.

constraint.text: Endpoint readiness should reflect serving eligibility without preventing StatefulSet recovery.

controls.title: Separate readiness from serving correctness
scenarios: Masterless limbo; crashed process during probe detection window; replica is Active but has wrong data.
assumptions: Readiness probes read assigned state and Kubernetes acts after configured delays.
residual_risks: Limbo deliberately reports Ready to break OrderedReady deadlock; headless addresses include NotReady pods; no content guarantee.
controls.call_path: kubelet exec readiness -> Pod Ready -> endpoint controller; OrderedReady also consumes readiness.

checks.procedure: Exercise limbo, restart ordering, direct headless clients and delayed endpoint removal; design an independent serving gate. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

review.note: Initial static audit. Existing code and prospective checks are not archived execution evidence; no safety verification is claimed.

constraint.text: Operational comparison should identify current source and each replica rather than infer from cluster-wide counts.

controls.title: Expose role-aware observations
scenarios: Role changes after failover while existing time series persist.
assumptions: Role metadata must track topology generations without mislabeling old samples.
residual_risks: No flared role labels; operator count comparison is a limited substitute.
controls.call_path: flared metrics exporter and operator topology metrics are separate sources; role-aware join is not implemented.

checks.procedure: Specify and test role changes in metrics, including stale series and all-replica comparison. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.
